description: A tropical climber famous for its glossy, split leaves. Native to the rainforests of southern Mexico, it grows fast and makes a dramatic statement indoors.

care.water: Every 1–2 weeks, when the top 5 cm of soil is dry

funFact: The holes (fenestrations) may help the leaves withstand strong winds and let light reach lower leaves.

description: A sculptural indoor tree with large, violin-shaped leaves. It loves consistency and will reward a stable spot with lush growth.

care.water: Weekly, when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry
care.light: Bright, filtered light; some direct morning sun
care.fertilizer: Every 4 weeks during the growing season

funFact: Fiddle leaf figs dislike being moved and may drop leaves after a change of location.

description: A forgiving trailing vine with heart-shaped, gold-marbled leaves. Perfect for shelves and hanging baskets.

care.water: Every 1–2 weeks; let soil dry halfway
care.fertilizer: Every 6–8 weeks in spring and summer

toxicity: Toxic to pets and humans if ingested
funFact: Pothos is nearly impossible to kill and stays green even in darker rooms.

description: Upright, sword-like leaves with striking banding. Extremely drought tolerant and a classic choice for beginners.

care.water: Every 2–4 weeks; let soil dry fully

funFact: Snake plants use CAM photosynthesis, opening their pores at night to save water.

description: Elegant dark-green foliage with white, hood-like blooms. It droops dramatically when thirsty and perks up quickly after watering.

care.fertilizer: Every 6 weeks in spring and summer

funFact: The white 'flower' is actually a modified leaf called a spathe.

description: A succulent with thick, gel-filled leaves, prized for its soothing sap. Thrives on neglect and sunshine.

care.light: Bright light with some direct sun

funFact: Aloe has been used medicinally for more than 6,000 years.

description: The classic flowering shrub, loved for its fragrant blooms in countless colours. Needs sun, air flow, and regular feeding.

care.water: Deeply 2–3 times per week in summer

funFact: The oldest known living rose is thought to be about 1,000 years old, growing on a cathedral in Germany.

description: A fragrant culinary herb with tender, bright-green leaves. Pinch flower buds to keep it bushy and productive.

care.water: Keep soil evenly moist; water at the base

funFact: Basil is part of the mint family, which is why its stems are square.

description: A productive fruiting vegetable that loves heat. Consistent watering and good air flow are key to healthy, tasty fruit.

care.water: Deep, consistent watering 2–3 times per week
care.fertilizer: Balanced feed, then high-potassium when fruiting

toxicity: Leaves and stems are toxic to pets
funFact: Botanically, a tomato is a berry.

description: A cool-season crop grown for its starchy tubers. Hilling soil around the stems protects tubers from light.
funFact: Potatoes were the first vegetable grown in space, in 1995.

description: A warm-season vegetable producing sweet, crunchy fruit that ripens from green to red, yellow, or orange.

care.water: 1–2 times per week; keep evenly moist

funFact: Red bell peppers are simply green peppers left to ripen longer.
